judgments.reason: A normal erythropoietin level does not clinically support secondary polycythemia; secondary polycythemia is typically associated with elevated erythropoietin. Normal EPO would more commonly point toward a primary (JAK2-driven) or congenital/hemoglobin-variant cause. The actual driver here is Hb Tak (a high-oxygen-affinity hemoglobin variant), which is not captured in the cited span, and the cited span itself argues against rather than for secondary polycythemia.
